title: Aurora
sub: Soft blue ribbons drift and fold
html:
Quietly alive.

Soft light, always moving.
prompt: Build an aurora background for a hero section. Make a full-bleed container with a pale sky gradient (white to very light blue). Inside it place three absolutely positioned ribbons, each about 160% of the container width and 30% of its height, with border-radius: 50%, a horizontal linear-gradient that fades to transparent at both ends, and filter: blur(20px). Each ribbon gets its own keyframes that combine translateX (about +-8%), a small rotate (-9deg to 6deg) and scaleY (0.8 to 1.55), with different durations between 9s and 12s, ease-in-out, infinite, so the ribbons drift past each other and fold. Animate transform only and add will-change: transform. Use soft sky blues plus one stronger accent ribbon at low opacity (0.55-0.8). Never use neon or purple. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Mesh gradient
sub: Four color points slowly shift
html:
Color, in motion.

A mesh that never repeats.
prompt: Build a mesh gradient background. Use a container with a light blue base color (#FFEFEA style, your palette) and four absolutely positioned layers, each about 95% wide and 120% tall, one near each corner. Each layer is a radial-gradient(closest-side, color, transparent) in a different tone: your strong accent at about 60% alpha, a mid sky blue, pure white, and a light blue. Animate each layer with its own transform keyframes (translate by 30-40% of its size plus a scale between 0.9 and 1.2), durations 15-20s, ease-in-out, infinite, so the four colors slowly trade places and the mesh never settles. Animate transform only, add will-change: transform, and keep the blending in the gradients rather than using mix-blend-mode or heavy blur filters, which keeps it cheap on mobile. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Dot grid spotlight
sub: Dots brighten around a moving light
html:
Follow the light.

Move your pointer over this card.
prompt: Build a dot grid background with a spotlight that follows the pointer. Layer one: a full-bleed element with background-image: radial-gradient(circle, a light grey-blue 1.3px, transparent 1.8px) and background-size: 16px 16px. Layer two: the same grid in your accent color, brighter and slightly larger dots, with mask-image: radial-gradient(circle 80px at var(--x) var(--y), #000, transparent) so only the dots near the light show. Add a faint radial-gradient glow at the same point. On pointermove update --x and --y on the container in a requestAnimationFrame callback (not on every event). When there is no pointer, drive --x and --y along a slow Lissajous path (sin with different frequencies) and yield to the real pointer for a couple of seconds after it moves. On touch devices keep the autoplay path. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Moving grid floor
sub: A perspective grid scrolls toward you
html:
Built to go far.

Infinite runway, zero effort.
prompt: Build a retro-clean perspective grid floor background. Make a horizon at about 46% of the container height: pale sky gradient above, with a soft sun disc (a circle with a white to light blue gradient) sitting on the horizon. Below it, a floor element with perspective: 220px and perspective-origin: 50% 0, overflow: hidden, and a mask-image: linear-gradient(transparent, #000 45%) so the grid fades into the horizon. Inside, one plane that is 220% wide and 400% tall, transform-origin: 50% 0, transform: rotateX(72deg), with two repeating 1.6px linear-gradient lines (horizontal and vertical) on a 30px background-size in a mid sky blue. Animate the plane with transform: rotateX(72deg) translateY(0) to translateY(30px) (exactly one cell), linear, 1.8s, infinite, so the loop is seamless and only transform animates. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Film grain
sub: Animated grain over a blue gradient
html:
Texture, not noise.

Grain that feels like film.
prompt: Build a film grain background over a blue gradient. Layer one is a slowly moving gradient: an oversized element (150% of the container) with two radial-gradients (a near-white highlight and a deeper accent blue) over a sky blue linear-gradient, animated with a gentle rotate and scale over about 16s, alternate. Layer two is the grain: an inline SVG with <filter><feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.85" numOctaves="2" stitchTiles="stitch"/><feColorMatrix type="saturate" values="0"/></filter> applied to a full-size rect, positioned slightly larger than the container, with opacity around 0.5 and mix-blend-mode: overlay. Animate the grain layer with a steps(1) keyframe that jumps its translate between five or six offsets once per second so it flickers like film, without re-running the filter. Keep the grain subtle; if text looks dirty, lower the opacity. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Floating blobs
sub: Blurred blobs float and merge
html: Weekly report
prompt: Build a floating blobs background behind a small glass card. Use a white container and four absolutely positioned circles of different sizes (26-46% of the container width), each filled with a flat blue from your palette (sky blue, light blue, accent) at 0.3-0.8 opacity, with filter: blur(16px). Give each its own transform keyframes that travel 40-90% of their own size in different directions and scale between 0.85 and 1.3, durations 11-16s, ease-in-out, infinite, so they drift into each other and the overlaps blend into new shades. Put the content (for example a card with background: rgba(255,255,255,.82) and a soft shadow) on top. Animate transform only; blur the elements statically, never animate the blur radius. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Particle drift
sub: Tiny dots float up with depth
html:
Rising quietly.

Depth without the weight.
prompt: Build a particle drift background with a canvas. Put a <canvas> absolutely positioned behind the content, sized from clientWidth and clientHeight times devicePixelRatio (capped at 2) and resized when the container changes. Create about 60-80 particles with a random depth value z from 0 to 1. Depth controls everything: radius (1px to 3.5px), opacity (0.14 to 0.64) and upward speed (slow for far, faster for near), plus a tiny horizontal sine sway. In a requestAnimationFrame loop move each particle up by speed times delta time, wrap it to the bottom with a new random x when it leaves the top, clearRect and draw filled circles in your accent color with rgba alpha. Skip all work while the tab or the section is hidden, and cap the delta time so a pause does not cause a jump. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Wave lines
sub: Stacked sine lines undulate
prompt: Build a wave lines background with SVG. Use one full-size <svg> with viewBox="0 0 400 300" and preserveAspectRatio="none". Draw five to seven <path> lines stacked about 26 units apart in the lower two thirds, each a sine wave generated as a polyline (y = y0 + amplitude * sin(x / period * 2 * PI + phase)) that is wider than the viewBox (0 to 800). Give each line its own period (150-260), amplitude (9-17) and a stroke from light sky blue to your accent with rising opacity, stroke-width 1.6 and vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke. Animate each path with transform: translateX(0) to translateX(-period) linear infinite at different speeds (9-18s); because the translate equals exactly one period the loop is seamless. Put the headline in the clear top third. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Constellation
sub: Nodes drift and link when near
html:
Everything connects.

Move over the card to join in.
prompt: Build a constellation background with a canvas. Spawn about 35-60 nodes with random positions and slow random velocities, bouncing at the edges. Each frame in requestAnimationFrame, move the nodes by velocity times delta time, then for every pair closer than roughly 30% of the shorter container side draw a 1px line whose alpha falls off linearly with distance (max about 0.4) in your accent color, then draw each node as a 2px filled circle. Treat the pointer as one extra node so lines reach toward the cursor. Size the canvas from clientWidth and clientHeight times devicePixelRatio (cap 2), cap the node count on small screens (O(n squared) pair checks), and cap the frame delta so a tab switch does not teleport the nodes. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Conic sweep
sub: A soft conic gradient rotates
html: Pro plan$12/moStart free trial
prompt: Build a conic sweep glow behind a pricing or feature card. Place an oversized circle (about 170% of the container width, centered with negative margins) behind the card with background: conic-gradient(from 0deg, white, light blue, sky blue, pale blue, mid blue, white) and a static filter: blur(26px), opacity about 0.8. Rotate it with transform: rotate(0) to rotate(360deg), linear, 16s, infinite, will-change: transform. Because the gradient is smooth and the element is blurred, the rotation reads as slow drifting light behind the card instead of a spinner. Put the card on top with a translucent white background (rgba(255,255,255,.88)), a 1px white inner border and a soft layered shadow. Do not animate the blur and do not use backdrop-filter over the rotating layer. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Moving stripes
sub: Thin diagonal stripes glide
html:
Smooth lines.

Thin, calm and in step.
prompt: Build a moving diagonal stripes background. Make a wrapper about 160% of the container size, centered, with transform: rotate(-28deg) and a radial mask (mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, #000 40%, transparent 95%)) so the stripes fade out toward the edges. Inside, stack two full-size layers. The first is a fine pattern, repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 22px, accent at 40% alpha 22px 24px); animate it with transform: translateX(0) to translateX(24px), linear, about 2.6s, infinite. The second is a wider, paler band pattern, repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 56px, light blue 56px 70px), animated the other way by exactly its period (translateX(-70px)) over 6s. Translating by exactly one pattern period makes the loop seamless, and only transform animates. Add will-change: transform. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Bokeh
sub: Soft circles of light fade in and out
html:
Soft focus.

Out of focus, never out of mind.
prompt: Build a bokeh background. Place 10-12 absolutely positioned circles of varied sizes (24-54px) around a pale blue gradient. Each circle uses radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, white at 95%, light blue at 38% alpha, accent at 12% alpha) plus a 1px inset white ring, which gives a glassy out-of-focus disc. Animate each with a keyframe from opacity 0, translateY(8px), scale(0.8), to opacity 0.9 around 35-60%, back to opacity 0 with translateY(-14px) scale(1.12), 7s ease-in-out infinite, with negative or positive animation-delay values staggered between 0 and 5s so the discs never fade in unison. Animate only transform and opacity. Keep the discs low contrast so the text on top stays readable. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Topographic
sub: Contour lines shift slowly
prompt: Build a topographic contour background with inline SVG. Generate two clusters of 8 nested closed paths in JS (or by hand). Each path is a smooth closed curve through about 16 points whose radius is r * (1 + 0.13 sin(2a + seed) + 0.08 sin(3a - 1.3 seed) + 0.04 sin(5a + 0.7 seed)), converted to cubic Beziers with Catmull-Rom control points; give each ring a slightly different seed so adjacent rings look related, like real contours. Stroke only: 1.1px in a pale blue, and every third ring 1.5px in a mid blue. Animate each ring with transform: scale(0.965) to scale(1.045) over 10s ease-in-out infinite using transform-box: fill-box and transform-origin: center, with negative animation-delay stepped per ring so the rings breathe in a ripple, and rotate each cluster very slowly (70-90s linear). Set vector strokes only, no fills, and keep the labels small and left aligned. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Ripples
sub: Rings expand from a point and fade
html:
Make an impact.

Every action travels outward.
prompt: Build a ripples background centered on a point, for example behind a "listening" or "live" section. Put a zero-size anchor at the point (for example left: 50%, top: 40%). Inside it add four ring elements, each a 150px circle with margin to center it, border: 1.5px solid a mid sky blue, opacity 0 and transform: scale(0.05). Animate each with a keyframe from opacity 0.8 and scale(0.05) to opacity 0 and scale(2.4), 4.8s, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.6, 0.3, 1), infinite, with animation-delay 0s, 1.2s, 2.4s and 3.6s so there is always a ring at a different stage. Add a solid 10px accent dot at the center with a soft 4px halo. Animate only transform and opacity. For an interactive version, spawn a new ring at the pointer on click and remove it on animationend. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Light beams
sub: Angled beams sweep across
html:
See it clearly.

Light that moves with you.
prompt: Build a light beams background. Use a sky blue gradient container (deeper blue at the top left fading to near white). Inside place a wrapper about 160% of the container size, centered, rotated 24deg. Add five tall beams of different widths (7-16% of the wrapper) at different left offsets, each filled with linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(255,255,255,.7), transparent). Animate each beam with a keyframe from translateX(-90%) with opacity 0.2 through translateX(90%) with opacity 0.9 and back, using different durations (9-12s) and negative delays so beams cross each other. ease-in-out, infinite. Animate transform and opacity only. Keep the beams soft (no hard edges, no blur filter needed) and place content in a clear central area. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Tile shimmer
sub: Squares light up in a traveling wave
html: All systems normal
prompt: Build a tile shimmer background. Make a CSS grid of 8 columns by 6 rows of white rounded squares (radius 7px, 6px gap, 1px inset hairline) covering the section. Give every tile an ::after overlay filled with your accent gradient and opacity 0. Animate the overlay with a keyframe where opacity is 0 at the start and the end and peaks at about 0.85 at 14%, back to 0 by 36%, duration 3.6s, ease-in-out, infinite, and set animation-delay per tile to (column + row) * 0.13s so the light travels as a diagonal wave. Set the delay with a CSS custom property per tile. Only opacity animates. Put a solid white pill with a soft shadow in the middle so the foreground stays readable over the lit tiles. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Morphing blob
sub: One SVG blob changes its shape
html:
Shape shifts.

One path, endless forms.
prompt: Build a morphing blob background with SVG and a small requestAnimationFrame loop (CSS cannot reliably interpolate path data across browsers). Draw one <path> in a square viewBox centered on the origin, filled with a light-to-mid sky blue linear-gradient, plus a second unfilled outline path with a 1px pale blue stroke behind it. Each frame compute 8 points around a circle, with radius = base * (1 + 0.13 sin(2a + 0.8t) + 0.09 sin(3a - 0.6t) + 0.05 sin(4a + 1.1t)), where a is the point angle and t is elapsed seconds. Convert the points to a closed cubic Bezier path with Catmull-Rom control points and set the d attribute. Use slow time factors so a full change takes 6-8 seconds. Cap the delta time, pause when offscreen, and give the SVG aria-hidden="true". Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Clouds parallax
sub: Cloud layers drift at different speeds
html:
Head in the clouds.

Layers that move at their own pace.
prompt: Build a clouds parallax background. Use a vertical sky gradient (mid sky blue at the top, near white at the bottom). Create three cloud layers, each a div twice the container width with the same set of inline SVG clouds (a single path made of circles, fill white) repeated in both halves, so translating the layer by -50% loops seamlessly. Far layer: small clouds, opacity 0.55, 80s. Middle layer: medium clouds, opacity 0.8, 46s. Near layer: large clouds low in the frame, opacity 0.95, 26s. All linear, infinite, transform: translateX(0) to translateX(-50%). The speed difference between layers sells the depth. Keep the headline in the clear sky area and make sure text stays readable when a near cloud passes behind it. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Isometric blocks
sub: Blocks rise and fall in a wave
html:
Built in layers.

Depth you can feel.
prompt: Build an isometric block grid background with SVG. Use a 6 by 6 grid of columns. Project each cell with x = cx + (i - j) * W and y = cy + (i + j) * W / 2, where W is the half width of a cell. Draw each column as three polygons: a top diamond, a left face and a right face, in three tones of one blue (very light top, light blue left, mid blue right) with a thin white stroke. Create the polygons in painter order (sorted by i + j ascending) so nearer columns overlap farther ones. In a requestAnimationFrame loop set the height of each column to 5 + 34 * k squared, where k = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t * 1.15 - (i + j) * 0.75), so a wave of rising and falling blocks travels diagonally. Highlight the tallest column with your accent blue. Update only the points attribute, pause offscreen, and cap the delta time. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

title: Radial glow
sub: A soft glow breathes behind a headline
html:
Calm by design.

It breathes about once every seven seconds.
prompt: Build a breathing radial glow behind a hero headline. Use a white container. Center two absolutely positioned circles: an inner one about 86% of the container width with radial-gradient(closest-side, accent-light at 42% alpha, 14% alpha at 55%, transparent), and an outer one about 130% wide with a much fainter radial-gradient of your accent at 12% alpha. Animate both with the same keyframes, transform: scale(0.94) with opacity 0.7 at the ends and scale(1.07) with opacity 1 at 50%, duration 7s, ease-in-out, infinite, with the outer one offset by half a cycle (negative delay of 3.5s). The amplitude must stay low: it should feel like breathing, not pulsing. Animate only transform and opacity, and place the headline above at z-index 1 with enough contrast over the brightest glow. Keep the content in a separate layer above the background (position: relative; z-index: 1) and check text contrast against the lightest and darkest moment of the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion stop the animation and show a still frame. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.
